content: Zinc gluconate is a lozenge that has been approved by the FDA for the treatment of the common cold. It is known to reduce the severity of cold symptoms, such as cough, sore throat, nasal congestion, sneezing, postnasal drip, and hoarseness. Common adverse reactions include stomach upset. For adults and children aged 12 years and older, it is recommended to begin treatment at the onset of symptoms, ideally within 24 to 48 hours. The lozenges should be dissolved completely in the mouth and not chewed. The recommended daily dosage is six lozenges for adults and four lozenges for individuals aged 12 to 17. Children under 12 years of age should consult a healthcare professional before use. There is limited information regarding off-label use of zinc gluconate in both adult and pediatric populations. Similarly, there is limited data on its use in specific populations, including pregnant or breastfeeding women, pediatric patients, geriatric patients, and immunocompromised individuals. There is also no FDA guidance on its use in patients with renal or hepatic impairment, or in relation to specific gender or racial populations. Zinc gluconate may interact with certain medications, such as minocycline, doxycycline, tetracycline, or warfarin (Coumadin). It may inhibit the absorption of these drugs. Patients are advised to consult a doctor before use if they are taking these medications. If symptoms persist beyond seven days, users should stop taking the product and consult a healthcare provider. Cold-EEZE® lozenges are formulated to reduce the duration of common cold symptoms but may not be sufficient for treating influenza or allergies. Diabetic patients should be aware that sugar replacements in the product may affect blood sugar levels. Pregnant or breastfeeding individuals should consult a healthcare professional before use. The product should be kept out of reach of children. Patients are advised to avoid dissolving the lozenges on an empty stomach to prevent minor stomach upset. Citrus fruits, juices, or products containing citric acid should be avoided for 30 minutes before or after taking the lozenges, as they may reduce the product's effectiveness. Otherwise, patients should drink plenty of fluids. The product is gluten-free but may produce a laxative effect. There is no established interaction between alcohol and zinc gluconate, but patients should discuss potential effects with their doctor. The product should be stored in a cool, dry place after opening. There is limited information available regarding clinical trial experience, postmarketing experience, pharmacodynamics, pharmacokinetics, nonclinical toxicology, and overdose of zinc gluconate. Additionally, there is no FDA guidance on its use during labor and delivery or in nursing mothers. The product is marketed under the brand name Cold-EEZE® and is clinically proven to reduce the duration of the common cold.
